facts.fact: Adwave's prepaid wallet accepts top-ups from $30 to $50,000, according to the page.
facts.quote: With Adwave, for example, the wallet takes anything from $30 to $50,000.

facts.fact: Omnisend's analysis, as cited on the page, found that marketers running campaigns across three or more channels saw a 287% higher purchase rate than single-channel campaigns.
facts.quote: saw a [287% higher purchase rate](https://www.omnisend.com/blog/omnichannel-statistics/) than single-channel campaigns

facts.fact: The page states that agency retainer contracts are usually 3 to 12 months long.
The page states that on prepaid platforms the advertiser is charged only for active days.
facts.quote: You're charged for active days only.

facts.fact: The page states that some channels, including streaming TV, previously required five-figure minimums before prepaid options existed.
facts.quote: That opens up channels, including streaming TV, that used to require five-figure minimums and a media buyer.

facts.fact: The page gives an example in which loading $500 with a $50 daily ceiling covers about ten active days of spend at maximum.
facts.quote: Say you load $500 and set a $50/day ceiling. Worst case, the platform spends the full $50 each active day, and your $500 lasts about ten active days

facts.fact: The page states that Google Ads and Meta run on postpaid billing by default, with the card charged after ad spend on a threshold or monthly cycle.
facts.quote: Self-serve giants like Google Ads and Meta run on postpaid billing by default: your card gets charged after your ads spend, on a threshold or monthly cycle

facts.fact: Adwave lets users fund a wallet from $30 to $50,000.
facts.quote: **Fund a wallet from $30 to $50,000.** Start as small as you want.

facts.fact: Adwave allows a daily budget to be set from $30 to $10,000 per day.
facts.quote: **Set a daily budget from $30 to $10,000/day.** A ceiling you control.

facts.fact: Adwave states that users are charged once per active day and the campaign pauses when the wallet runs out.
facts.quote: You're charged once per active day, and the campaign pauses when the wallet's dry, so you can never go into debt.

facts.fact: Adwave states it has no subscriptions and no contracts, with business campaign creative made in the app included; optional creation extras and card processing fees are separate.
facts.quote: **No subscriptions, no contracts.** Business campaign creative made in the app is included. Optional creation extras and card processing fees are separate.

facts.fact: Adwave states that undelivered budget is never charged and a launch that fails on day one is refunded in full.
facts.quote: Undelivered budget is never charged, and a launch that fails on day one is refunded in full.

facts.fact: Adwave's example suggests funding at least a couple weeks of the daily ceiling, with a $500 wallet at a $30/day ceiling giving roughly two-plus weeks of runway.
facts.quote: If you set a $30/day ceiling, a $500 wallet gives you roughly two-plus weeks of runway to see what's working

facts.fact: Adwave's prepaid wallet is described as one budget spanning web, TV, Google, Meta, and Reddit.
facts.quote: Adwave works this way: one budget spans web, TV, Google, Meta, and Reddit, so you get the reach of a multi-channel campaign without juggling five balances.

facts.fact: Adwave states that a small wallet of as little as $30 is enough to begin, with a daily ceiling as low as $30/day.
facts.quote: Adwave, for instance, lets you fund a wallet from as little as $30 and set a daily ceiling as low as $30/day.

facts.fact: The article states that Google and Meta default to postpaid billing, where ad spend occurs before the card is charged on a threshold or monthly cycle.
facts.quote: Google and Meta default to postpaid billing: your ads spend first, then your card gets charged on a threshold or monthly cycle.
